L01 | Deciding how much evidence is enough for the claim at hand, and how plainly to flag a thin base without burying the point, still depends on the stakes and the listener.
L02 | Choosing which actual outcome to inspect and how deep to look, such as a sample or every record, is still a call about what a failure would cost.
L03 | Knowing which single check is the deciding one for this piece of work is still a matter of understanding what "done" means here.
L04 | Deciding which things count as "beside" the fix and how far outward to look before stopping is still discretion.
L05 | Recognising that a person is asking for presence and not a solution, and sensing when that need has changed, is still a matter of reading the person.
L06 | Deciding whether another source could change the answer owed, and when the search has gone far enough, is still a call made case by case.
L07 | Deciding when a cause is established firmly enough to name, and when a paraphrase has become stronger than the original, is still interpretation.
L08 | Deciding how much testing a remembered fact deserves, and which nearby caveats must travel with it, still depends on how the fact will be used.
L09 | Deciding which work is important enough to need an outside reviewer, which reviewer is different in the way that matters, and how to weigh their corrections is still discretion.
L10 | Choosing which deliberate failure would truly prove that the test or monitor watches the right thing is still a matter of understanding what it is meant to catch.
L11 | Deciding how long to investigate before acting, when a wrong reading and a real loss call for opposite moves, is still a weighing of risk under time pressure.
L12 | Working out what an empty or short result actually says about the search, and what further evidence would justify a claim about the world, is still interpretation.
L13 | Deciding what counts as a source truly outside yourself, and whether it is reliable enough to justify the word "checked", is still a call.
L14 | Deciding what observable behaviour would show the setting is really in effect, and how long to wait to see it, is still judgment.
L15 | Deciding which lessons deserve a permanent step, where that step belongs, and when it has outlived its use is still a matter of weighing cost against risk.
L16 | Deciding which strings are long or important enough to require the program, and noticing when the program's source is itself wrong, is still judgment.
L17 | Deciding which clock and time zone are the right reference, and what to write when the event happened earlier than the moment of writing, is still judgment.
